questions.title: Predict on a game day
questions.prompt:
Fitted practice model from 312 observed days in the supplied workbook: Sales = 1044.415479 + (0.619594 × PriorYearSales) + (387.029626 × GameDay) + (0.01074 × PriorYearSales × GameDay). GameDay is 1 on listed game days and 0 otherwise. Sales and PriorYearSales use netTotal and netTotal_364 aggregated by date. Use these displayed coefficients.

Predict sales when PriorYearSales = 1000 and GameDay = 1. Round to two decimals. This is a supplied-input practice scenario, not an actual seven-day-ahead forecast.
questions.subject: Interpretation
questions.source: 1. Excel part 4/Regression Assignment/Restaurant/Instructions.docx · prediction and interaction tasks
questions.hint: Substitute into all four terms, including the interaction.

questions.title: Interpret a conditional slope
questions.prompt:
Fitted practice model from 312 observed days in the supplied workbook: Sales = 1044.415479 + (0.619594 × PriorYearSales) + (387.029626 × GameDay) + (0.01074 × PriorYearSales × GameDay). GameDay is 1 on listed game days and 0 otherwise. Sales and PriorYearSales use netTotal and netTotal_364 aggregated by date. Use these displayed coefficients.

Explain what the coefficient of PriorYearSales means, and how its meaning changes on a game day.
questions.subject: Interpretation
questions.source: 1. Excel part 4/Regression Assignment/Restaurant/Instructions.docx · final interaction task
questions.hint: Check the requested population, grouping level and units.
questions.solution: The non-game-day slope is 0.619594; the game-day slope is 0.630334. A one-unit increase in prior-year sales is associated with these changes in predicted current sales in the fitted model.
rubric: The main slope applies when GameDay = 0.
On a game day the slope is the main slope plus the interaction coefficient.
Describe an association in sales units, not a proven causal effect.

questions.title: The game-day contrast
questions.prompt:

GameDay is 1 on listed game days and 0 otherwise. Sales and PriorYearSales use netTotal and netTotal_364 aggregated by date. Use these displayed coefficients.

questions.subject: Interpretation
questions.source: 1. Excel part 4/Regression Assignment/Restaurant/Instructions.docx · game-day and interaction tasks
questions.hint: Check the requested population, grouping level and units.
questions.solution: The contrast is 387.029626 + 0.01074×1000 = 397.77. The main GameDay coefficient alone applies only at PriorYearSales = 0.

questions.title: Communicate confidence
questions.prompt: Bob needs a sales forecast seven days beyond the last observed day. Explain what future inputs you would need and why a fitted regression does not guarantee accurate sales predictions.
questions.subject: Interpretation
questions.source: 1. Excel part 4/Regression Assignment/Restaurant/Instructions.docx · prediction and communication tasks
questions.hint: Check the requested population, grouping level and units.
questions.solution: Use known calendar/game information and historical sales; obtain or explicitly assume other future inputs. Evaluate forecast errors on held-out dates. Explain uncertainty and its implications for staffing and ingredients.
rubric: Specify the forecast date and aggregate sales target.
Use inputs genuinely available at forecast time; do not use future realised sales or weather.
Discuss model fit, forecast errors and unusual days.
Separate association from causal claims and explain operational implications.

Simple fitted practice model from 312 matched days: Sales = 2725.292435 + (7.579688 × tmax). tmax is maximum daily temperature in the source weather data (°F); Sales is daily aggregate netTotal. Use the displayed coefficients.

Predict sales for tmax = 60°F. Round to two decimals.
questions.subject: Interpretation

questions.hint: Check the requested population, grouping level and units.

questions.title: Temperature slope
questions.prompt:
Simple fitted practice model from 312 matched days: Sales = 2725.292435 + (7.579688 × tmax). tmax is maximum daily temperature in the source weather data (°F); Sales is daily aggregate netTotal. Use the displayed coefficients.

Interpret the slope in context. Can you conclude that changing temperature causes sales to change?
questions.subject: Interpretation
questions.source: 1. Excel part 4/Regression Assignment/Restaurant/Instructions.docx · temperature task
questions.hint: Check the requested population, grouping level and units.
questions.solution: One additional degree Fahrenheit is associated with 7.579688 units of daily sales in this fitted model. Observational association does not establish causation or statistical significance.
rubric: State the predicted sales change for one additional degree Fahrenheit.
Describe association rather than causation.
Acknowledge omitted factors and uncertainty; coefficients alone do not establish significance.

questions.title: A ten-degree comparison
questions.prompt:
Simple fitted practice model from 312 matched days: Sales = 2725.292435 + (7.579688 × tmax). tmax is maximum daily temperature in the source weather data (°F); Sales is daily aggregate netTotal. Use the displayed coefficients.

What is the model's predicted change in sales when tmax rises from 50°F to 60°F? Round to two decimals.
questions.subject: Interpretation
questions.source: 1. Excel part 4/Regression Assignment/Restaurant/Instructions.docx · temperature task
questions.hint: Check the requested population, grouping level and units.
questions.solution: Subtract the two predictions. The intercept cancels: 10×7.579688 = 75.80.

questions.title: Prepare the restaurant data
questions.prompt: Explain how you would combine salesData, weatherData and gameData for a daily-sales regression without multiplying records or losing non-game days.

questions.solution: Aggregate sales by date, check uniqueness of date in auxiliary tables, and left-join on date. Record the assumption that an absent game-date record means no game; inspect missing weather before fitting.
rubric: Aggregate product-level sales to date.
Check one weather/game record per date before joining.
Preserve sales dates and treat absent scheduled game dates as non-game days under an explicit assumption.
Check missing weather and reconcile rows and total sales.
